full_judgment: 4. Mr. Abdul Malek appearing for the petitioners contended that the language of sub-clause (b) of clause (2) of Article 103 of the Constitution is plain and unambiguous and the expression "sentenced a person to death or to transportation for life" occurring therein means that the High Court Division has itself imposed one or the other sentenced mentioned therein and the imposition of such sentence may be in exercise of the original jurisdiction or by enhancement of the sentence of trial Court or by replacement of death sentence passed by the trial Court by a sentence of transportation for life or by the imposition of such sentences after reversal of an order of acquittal. According to him when a Sessions Judge passes a sentence of death under section 302 of the Penal Code and the High Court Division rejects he reference and replaces the death sentence by a sentence of transportation for life, the sentence which the person will suffer is the sentence passed by the High Court Division and the appeal in such a case will lie to this Division as of right under sub-clause (b) of clause (2) of Article 103.
